children.name: Passer
children.description: Intimately associated with human settlement for thousands of years. The House Sparrow has declined catastrophically in western European cities since the 1990s, including Stockholm, probably due to loss of nest sites in modernised buildings and reduced invertebrate food for chicks. The Tree Sparrow is slightly more rural, identified by its chestnut crown and black ear spot.

children.name: Passer domesticus
children.description: The house sparrow is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world. It is a small bird that has a typical length of 16 cm (6.3 in) and a mass of 24–39.5 g (0.85–1.39 oz). Females and young birds are coloured pale brown and grey, and males have brighter black, white, and brown markings.

children.name: Passer montanus
children.description: The tree sparrow is a passerine bird in the sparrow family with a rich chestnut crown and nape and a black patch on each pure white cheek. The sexes have similar plumage, and young birds are duller versions of the adult. This sparrow breeds across much of temperate Eurasia and Southeast Asia and has been introduced elsewhere, including the United States, where it is known as the Eurasian tree sparrow or German sparrow to differentiate it from the native American tree sparrow.

children.name: Passer ammodendri
children.description: The saxaul sparrow (Passer ammodendri) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family (Passeridae), found in parts of Central Asia.

children.name: Passer castanopterus
children.description: The Somali sparrow (Passer castanopterus) is a species of bird in the family Passeridae found in Somalia, Djibouti, Ethiopia and Kenya.

children.name: Passer cordofanicus
children.description: The Kordofan sparrow (Passer cordofanicus), also known as the Kordofan rufous sparrow, is a sparrow found only in southwestern Sudan and adjacent border regions of South Sudan and Chad.

children.name: Passer diffusus
children.description: The southern grey-headed sparrow (Passer diffusus) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae. It is sometimes treated as a subspecies of the grey-headed sparrow. It is found in savanna and woodland in Angola and Zambia southwards into South Africa, where it is expanding its range and is kept as a caged bird, like its relative the white-rumped seedeater.

children.name: Passer eminibey
children.description: The chestnut sparrow (Passer eminibey) is a species of passerine bird in the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer euchlorus
children.description: The Arabian golden sparrow (Passer euchlorus) is a sparrow found in south west Arabia and also the coast of Somalia and Djibouti where it occurs in thorn savannah and scrub habitats. It is sometimes considered as a subspecies of the Sudan golden sparrow (Passer luteus).

children.name: Passer flaveolus
children.description: The plain-backed sparrow (Passer flaveolus), also called the Pegu sparrow or olive-backed sparrow, is a sparrow found in Southeast Asia. Its range spans from Myanmar to central Vietnam, and south to the western part of Peninsular Malaysia.

children.name: Passer gongonensis
children.description: The parrot-billed sparrow (Passer gongonensis) is found in the arid lowlands of eastern Africa. At and, it is the largest of the sparrows of the family Passeridae. It is often considered a subspecies of the grey-headed sparrow.

children.name: Passer griseus
children.description: The northern grey-headed sparrow (Passer griseus), also known as the grey-headed sparrow, is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae, which is resident in much of tropical Africa.

children.name: Passer hemileucus
children.description: The Abd al-Kuri sparrow (Passer hemileucus) is a passerine bird endemic to the small island of Abd al Kuri. The sparrows are located primarily in the Socotra archipelago of the Indian Ocean, in Yemen, which is off the Horn of Africa. Their environment consists of shrubland and rocky areas with inland cliffs and mountain peaks. Though this species was originally described as a distinct species, it was considered conspecific with the Socotra sparrow. The sparrow is also referred to by its English name, Abd al-Kuri, or its Dutch, Middle Name, Abd al-Kuri Mus. A study by Guy Kirwan suggested that there are differences between the Abd al-Kuri sparrow and the Socotra sparrow. On the evidence that it is morphologically distinct, BirdLife International (and hence the IUCN Red List) recognised it as a species, and it was listed in the IOC World Bird List from December 2009. It has a restricted distribution, and a population of under 1,000 individuals.

children.name: Passer hispaniolensis
children.description: The Spanish sparrow or willow sparrow (Passer hispaniolensis) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer iagoensis
children.description: The Iago sparrow (Passer iagoensis), also known as the Cape Verde or rufous-backed sparrow, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer insularis
children.description: The Socotra sparrow (Passer insularis) is a passerine bird endemic to the islands of Socotra, Samhah, and Darsah in the Indian Ocean, off the Horn of Africa.

children.name: Passer italiae
children.description: The Italian sparrow (Passer italiae), also known as the cisalpine sparrow, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in Italy and other parts of the Mediterranean region.

children.name: Passer luteus
children.description: The Sudan golden sparrow (Passer luteus) is a small species of bird in the sparrow family found in sub-Saharan Africa. It is a famous cage bird, and in aviculture, it is known as the golden song sparrow. The Arabian golden sparrow and this species are sometimes considered one species, as the "golden sparrow".

children.name: Passer melanurus
children.description: The Cape sparrow (Passer melanurus), or mossie, is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae found in southern Africa.

children.name: Passer moabiticus
children.description: The Dead Sea sparrow (Passer moabiticus) is a species of bird in the Old World sparrow family Passeridae, with one subspecies breeding in parts of the West Asia and another in western Afghanistan and eastern Iran. The eastern subspecies P. M. Yatii is sometimes considered a separate species known as Yate's sparrow.

children.name: Passer motitensis
children.description: The great sparrow (Passer motitensis), also known as the southern rufous sparrow, is found in southern Africa in dry, wooded savannah and towns.

children.name: Passer pyrrhonotus
children.description: The Sind sparrow (Passer pyrrhonotus) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family, Passeridae, found around the Indus valley region in South Asia.

children.name: Passer rufocinctus
children.description: The Kenya sparrow (Passer rufocinctus), also known as the Kenya rufous sparrow, is a sparrow found in Kenya and Tanzania.

children.name: Passer cinnamomeus
children.description: The russet sparrow (Passer cinnamomeus), also called the cinnamon or cinnamon tree sparrow, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer shelleyi
children.description: Shelley's sparrow (Passer shelleyi), also known as Shelley's rufous sparrow or the White Nile rufous sparrow, is a sparrow found in eastern Africa from South Sudan, southern Ethiopia, and north-western Somalia to northern Uganda and north-western Kenya. Formerly, it was considered as a subspecies of the Kenya sparrow. This species is named after English geologist and ornithologist George Ernest Shelley.

children.name: Passer simplex
children.description: The desert sparrow (Passer simplex) is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae, found in the Sahara Desert of northern Africa.

children.name: Passer suahelicus
children.description: The Swahili sparrow (Passer suahelicus) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Passer swainsonii
children.description: The Swainson's sparrow (Passer swainsonii) is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae. Sometimes considered a subspecies of the grey-headed sparrow, it occurs in northeastern Africa, largely in the Ethiopian Highlands. This sparrow was named after the English naturalist and illustrator William Swainson.

children.name: Passer zarudnyi
children.description: Zarudny's sparrow (Passer zarudnyi), also known as the Asian desert sparrow, is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae, which occurs in Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, and formerly in Iran. This species has historically been classified as a subspecies of the desert sparrow, which is otherwise restricted to Africa. However, the species has a number of differences with the African species, including very similar plumage in adult males and females, which suggests this species is distinct enough to be considered separate, and possibly not most closely related to the African birds. Consequently, Zarudny's sparrow is treated as a separate species by BirdLife International, the IOC World Bird List, and the Handbook of the Birds of the World Alive.

children.name: Gymnoris
children.description: The bush sparrows or rock sparrows, a group of four Afrotropical and Asian species. They are medium-sized sparrows with relatively long tails and pale bills. Males typically have a yellow throat patch, especially conspicuous during the breeding season.

children.name: Gymnoris pyrgita
children.description:
The yellow-spotted bush sparrow or yellow-spotted petronia (Gymnoris pyrgita) is a species of bird in the sparrow family, Passeridae.
It is common throughout the Sahel and the Horn of Africa. Its natural habitats are dry savannah and subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland.

children.name: Gymnoris superciliaris
children.description: The yellow-throated bush sparrow (Gymnoris superciliaris), also known as the yellow-throated petronia, is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae. It is found in south-central and southern Africa in its natural habitats of subtropical or tropical dry forests, dry savanna, and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

children.name: Gymnoris dentata
children.description: The Sahel bush sparrow (Gymnoris dentata) or bush petronia, is a species of bird in the family Passeridae. It is found in Africa from Mauritania to Guinea and east to Eritrea and the south-western Arabian Peninsula in its natural habitats of dry savanna and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

children.name: Gymnoris xanthocollis
children.description: The yellow-throated sparrow or chestnut-shouldered petronia (Gymnoris xanthocollis) is a species of sparrow found in southern Asia. It is a species mostly of the dry savannah. They forage on the ground for grain and for berries in bushes. They are often seen perched atop bare branches on trees while calling.

children.name: Petronia
children.description: The Rock Sparrow is the sole member of this genus, a sturdy, streaked bird of rocky hillsides and open stony terrain across southern Europe, North Africa, and Asia. It has a pale bill and a distinctive yellow patch on the breast that is often hard to see.

children.name: Petronia petronia
children.description: The rock sparrow or rock petronia (Petronia petronia) is a small passerine bird in the sparrow family Passeridae.

children.name: Carpospiza
children.description: The Pale Rockfinch is the only species in this genus, a pale, finch-like bird of arid rocky hillsides. It has a thin bill compared to other sparrows and a soft, lark-like song. It breeds from Turkey east to Afghanistan and winters in northeastern Africa.

children.name: Carpospiza brachydactyla
children.description: The pale rockfinch or pale rock sparrow (Carpospiza brachydactyla) is a small sparrow found in the Middle East and Central Asia.

children.name: Hypocryptadius
children.description: The Cinnamon Ibon is an enigmatic passerine endemic to the mountains of Mindanao in the Philippines. Long considered a white-eye, molecular studies have firmly placed it within Passeridae as the most basal sparrow lineage. It forages in forest canopies for insects and fruit.

children.name: Hypocryptadius cinnamomeus
children.description: The cinnamon ibon (Hypocryptadius cinnamomeus) is a species of bird endemic to the mountains of Mindanao in the Philippines.

children.name: Montifringilla
children.description: The snowfinches — sturdy, pale-bodied birds of high-altitude plateaus and mountain slopes. They are well-adapted to cold environments with extensive white in the wings and tail that is flashed in flight. They occur across the high mountains of southern Europe, Central Asia, and the Tibetan Plateau.

children.name: Montifringilla nivalis
children.description: The white-winged snowfinch (Montifringilla nivalis) is a small passerine bird. Despite its name, it is a sparrow rather than a true finch.

children.name: Montifringilla adamsi
children.description:
The black-winged snowfinch or Adams's snowfinch (Montifringilla adamsi), is a species of bird in the sparrow family.
It is found in China, India, Nepal, and Pakistan. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland. It is commonly resident in the Tibetan plateau region of north-western Nepal, where it spends the summer at elevations of and the winter, on open stony hillsides, on plateau and near villages.

children.name: Montifringilla henrici
children.description: The Tibetan snowfinch or Henri's snowfinch (Montifringilla henrici) is a species of bird in the sparrow family.

children.name: Onychostruthus
children.description: The White-rumped Snowfinch is the sole species in this genus, distinguished from Montifringilla by its white rump and unique tail feather structure. It is a high-altitude specialist of the Tibetan Plateau, well-camouflaged against the rocky scree it inhabits.

children.name: Onychostruthus taczanowskii
children.description: The white-rumped snowfinch (Onychostruthus taczanowskii) is a species of passerine bird in the sparrow family Passeridae. It is the only member of the genus Onychostruthus. It is sometimes placed in the genus Montifringilla. It is found in Tibet and central-northern China. Its natural habitats are rocky areas in mountainous regions.

children.name: Pyrgilauda
children.description: The ground snowfinches — four small, pale snowfinch species that inhabit the high-altitude steppes and rocky slopes of Central Asia and the Tibetan Plateau. They are more terrestrial than Montifringilla and have less white in the wings. Named after the Greek pyrgos (tower) and lauda (lark), reflecting their ground-dwelling habits.

children.name: Pyrgilauda theresae
children.description: The Afghan snowfinch (Pyrgilauda theresae) or the Afghan ground-sparrow, bar-tailed snowfinch, Meinertzhagen's snowfinch, or Theresa's snowfinch, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, endemic to the northern parts of the Hindu Kush mountains in Afghanistan.

children.name: Pyrgilauda ruficollis
children.description: The rufous-necked snowfinch (Pyrgilauda ruficollis) is a species of bird in the sparrow family.

children.name: Pyrgilauda davidiana
children.description:
Père David's snowfinch (Pyrgilauda davidiana), also known as the small snowfinch, is a species of bird in the sparrow family.
It is found in Mongolia, southern Siberia and northern China. Its natural habitat is temperate grassland.

children.name: Pyrgilauda blanfordi
children.description:
Blanford's snowfinch (Pyrgilauda blanfordi) or the plain-backed snowfinch, is a species of bird in the sparrow family.
It is found in China, India, Nepal, and Pakistan. Its natural habitat is temperate grassland.
